source.title: [Paper] A is for Absorption: Studying Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a complete LessWrong summary post with comments, not the linked arXiv paper; it omits technical details from the paper.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports evidence that SAE latents can fail to fire on examples they appear to represent, while token-aligned latents absorb information and mediate the task instead. This challenges clean feature splitting and refines it as asymmetric absorption.
record.gate_note: The post reports first-letter task results and absorption findings. It also discusses traditional feature splitting, but does not report a direct measurement showing that larger dictionaries replace a coarse feature with a set of nearby, input-partitioning features. Comments proposing mechanisms or future work are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: This is the LessWrong summary of arXiv:2409.14507, which is an original source of the claim and the source of V4. It reports that first-letter latents in Gemma Scope SAEs on Gemma-2-2b miss valid tokens, that token-aligned latents absorb the feature, and that absorption persists across SAE size and sparsity. Because it is V4's original source, it gets no verdicts.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is largely right. The authors also attribute absorption to the sparsity-plus-reconstruction objective on co-occurring dense and sparse features. They stress that it reflects measurement error in SAEs, not how the model represents letters, since linear probes recover the feature. Evidence is limited to Gemma-2-2b, JumpReLU SAEs and one task.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a first-letter identification task and causal-mediation measurements on Gemma-2-2b Gemma Scope JumpReLU SAEs to study absorption, rather than directly measuring clean coarse-to-fine feature splitting.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported absorption rate varies with SAE size and sparsity.
record.problems: The post limits the evidence to Gemma-2-2b, JumpReLU SAEs, and the first-letter task. It gives no numerical results, per-size or per-sparsity values, uncertainty estimates, or detailed results by SAE; the post itself notes that broader validation is future work.

untested.parts: Coarse-to-fine replacement with dictionary growth, coverage of inputs by child features, and directional proximity. The 'starts with L' split is only an illustrative example.
Large models and SAE families beyond Gemma Scope JumpReLU on Gemma-2-2b.
Nested, geometrically close feature families mirroring a concept hierarchy.
Decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and novel latents in larger SAEs.
The authors only hypothesise that absorption is a 'pathological strategy' for the sparsity objective. No alternative objective, such as Matryoshka SAEs, is compared.

missing.what: Quantitative absorption rates, precision/recall against probes, and per-width/L0/layer breakdowns from the full paper. The post summarises these only qualitatively.
Bloom's comment on absorption by non-token-aligned latents, e.g. an 'assistance' latent absorbing both 'a' and 'h'.
missing.locator: Comment by Joseph Bloom replying to Joseph Miller

record.verdict_notes: The study is an original source for V4 (the same paper as arXiv:2409.14507), so no verdict labels are given. The text is a blog summary without numbers. The record's V6 links are removed because sweeping size or sparsity is not a test of alternative objectives.

versions.untested_parts: No direct test of coarse-to-fine replacement, input coverage by the proposed child features, or directional proximity.
The post reports Gemma-2-2b and Gemma Scope SAEs, not large models or a range of models and open SAE releases.
No test of nested feature families or whether they mirror a hierarchy of concepts.
The post does not give per-feature quantitative results or test whether changing size or sparsity eliminates absorption in every setting.
No comparison testing whether larger latents decompose into smaller latents or whether larger SAEs add novel latents.

The post varies SAE sparsity but does not compare alternative training objectives, including Matryoshka SAEs, or establish that the effect is caused by the objective rather than the model's representations.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Measured first-letter information tracked by SAE latents and compared its precision and recall with linear probes.
rows.measure: Precision and recall of SAE latents tracking first-letter information
rows.value: SAE latents were much worse classifiers than linear probes; no numerical values stated.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative comparison across the reported SAE experiment; the post does not give separate values by SAE, layer, or dictionary width.
rows.check: This is the headline result that SAE latents are much worse classifiers than linear probes. The authors attribute this to absorption, so for V4 it is observed, not partial. No numbers are given in the post.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Checked whether apparently interpretable first-letter latents activated on valid examples and identified latents that absorbed the feature.
rows.measure: Activation of the apparent first-letter latent on examples it should cover
rows.value: Some apparent feature latents failed to activate on seemingly arbitrary valid examples, such as an “Elephant” example for a starts-with-E feature.
rows.note: The post describes this as a qualitative result and gives an example, not a rate.
rows.check: The implicit baseline is the ground-truth first-letter label, with the linear probe as reference. The result is qualitative, an example rather than a rate.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Identified latents that weakly projected onto the feature direction and mediated the task in place of the apparent main latent.
rows.measure: Projection onto the feature direction and causal mediation by absorbing latents
rows.value: Absorbing latents weakly projected onto the feature direction and causally mediated in place of the main latent.
rows.note: The post says causal interventions are built into its absorption metric but provides no numerical results here.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Varied SAE dictionary size and measured the rate of feature absorption.
rows.value: The rate of absorption varies with SAE size; the post says tuning is unlikely to remove absorption entirely. No numerical values stated.
rows.locator: Feature Absorption is problematic; summary of hyperparameter results
rows.note: The post does not state the specific sizes or how the absorption rate changes across them.
rows.check: Varying SAE width is not a change of training objective, so the V6 link should be removed. For V4: absorption rate varies with size but is 'likely robust to tuning'; no values given.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Varied SAE sparsity and measured the rate of feature absorption.
rows.value: The rate of absorption varies with sparsity; the post says tuning is unlikely to remove absorption entirely. No numerical values stated.
rows.locator: Feature Absorption is problematic; summary of hyperparameter results
rows.note: The post does not state the specific sparsity settings or the direction or size of the rate changes.
rows.check: Varying sparsity within the JumpReLU objective does not test V6's claim about alternative objectives, so the V6 link should be removed. No values given.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2b
rows.operation_detail: Reported cases of partial absorption in which the main latent still fired and both it and the absorbing latent affected the spelling task under ablation.
rows.measure: Main-latent activation and ablation effect of main and absorbing latents
rows.value: Some partial-absorption cases had a weakly firing main latent; both the absorbing latent and the main latent had positive cosine similarity with the probe direction and an ablation effect on the spelling task.
rows.note: This is an author comment describing cases also seen in the work, not a quantified result in the post summary.
rows.check: The source is an author's comment, not the post body or the paper. The paper's own absorption metric excludes these partial cases.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
